milestones.text: Cygnus Solutions is co-founded as the first enterprise-grade commercial support provider for free software.
Bob Young establishes ACC Corporation to distribute Linux and UNIX computer accessories.
Marc Ewing releases “Halloween” Red Hat Linux, establishing the brand and trademark.

eras.title: Corporate formation and the public market

milestones.text: Bob Young merges ACC Corp with Marc Ewing's business, forming Red Hat Software.
Red Hat establishes the Red Hat Center for Open Source to advocate for public domain resources and intellectual property reform.
Launches the Red Hat Certified Engineer (RHCE) program, establishing the industry's first standard for open-source technical credentials.
Red Hat goes public (IPO) on Wall Street.
Red Hat acquires Cygnus Solutions for $674 million.

eras.title: Enterprise platform pivot and Fedora upstream

milestones.text: Launches Red Hat Network (RHN), introducing automated software patch delivery.
Launches Red Hat Linux Advanced Server, shifting the company from retail boxed products to enterprise subscription models.
Official release of Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL).
Establishes the Fedora Project, creating a community-governed distribution to act as RHEL's upstream testing ground.
Hosts the inaugural annual Red Hat Summit in New Orleans.
Acquires JBoss, expanding Red Hat's portfolio into enterprise Java middleware.
Acquires Qumranet, bringing KVM (Kernel-based Virtual Machine) technology natively into Linux.
Co-founds Open Source for America to advocate for open-source adoption within the Federal Government.

eras.title: Pivoting to cloud and standardizing the OSPO

milestones.text: Launches opensource.com to write about open-source methodologies across business and technology.
Launches CloudForms and OpenShift Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS).
Formally structures the Open Source and Standards (OSAS) team to centralize community stewardship.
Sponsors the CentOS Project and hires its core developers.
Red Hat's OSAS team co-founds the Linux Foundation's TODO Group to codify OSPO best practices.

eras.title: Enterprise container platforms and the hybrid cloud anchor

milestones.text: Acquires container operating system pioneer CoreOS.
Formalizes and renames OSAS to the Open Source Program Office (OSPO), operating directly under the Office of the CTO.
Launches RHEL 8 and re-platforms OpenShift 4 to run natively on automated Kubernetes and CoreOS.
IBM completes its acquisition of Red Hat for $34 billion.

eras.title: Scaling hybrid platforms and democratizing AI

milestones.text: Launches RHEL 9 to optimize hybrid multi-cloud and edge infrastructure deployments.
Red Hat launches Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI (RHEL AI) and packages indemnified IBM Granite LLMs.
Launches the InstructLab project in collaboration with IBM Research, enabling community-driven open-source LLM model alignment.

eras.title: Scaling agentic AI and secure supply chains

milestones.text: Releases Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 (RHEL 10).
Releases Red Hat AI 3, introducing distributed AI inference and agentic AI platforms.
Joins the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) as a Gold Member to integrate Model Context Protocol (MCP) standards.
Launches Red Hat AI 3.4 and Red Hat Desktop for local AI agent environments at Red Hat Summit.
Red Hat and IBM initiate Project Lightwell, a $5 billion engineering program deploying AI systems to defend open-source supply chains.
Launches Project Akrites alongside tech leaders to secure upstream repositories against AI-generated security exploits.
